conventions.rho: L = -(g_rho/2) Nbar [gamma^mu rho_mu . tau - (kappa_rho/(2M)) sigma^{mu nu} d_nu rho_mu . tau] N  (tau/2 convention; g_rho = universal coupling = g_rho-pi-pi). Hartree, homogeneous: eps_rho = C_rho n^2 delta^2/8, C_rho = g_rho^2/m_rho^2, S_rho = C_rho n/8, V_rho(neutron/proton) = +- C_rho n delta/4, delta = (n_n - n_p)/n. (Session convention, gauge_isovector.py / nvg_isospin_jet_audit.py.)  The tensor term has no Hartree contribution in homogeneous matter.
conventions.delta: L = -g_delta Nbar tau . delta N (full-tau convention of the Bonn OBE potentials).  Field variable D = g_delta delta_3 [MeV]: M*_n = M y - D, M*_p = M y + D, eps_delta = D^2/(2 C_delta), C_delta = g_delta^2/m_delta^2, stationarity D = C_delta (n_s,n - n_s,p).
conventions.functional: eps(n_n, n_p; y, D) = F_F(n_n, M y - D) + F_F(n_p, M y + D) + U(y) + C_v n^2/(2 y^2) + C_rho n^2 delta^2/(8 y^(2a)) + D^2/(2 C_delta); a = 0 (constant m_rho) or a = 1 (m_rho = q_rho W = m_rho y); y and D re-stationarised (both minimise); P = n_n mu_n + n_p mu_p - eps (no rearrangement terms: all fields stationary).
conventions.S2_analytic: S_2(n) = k_F^2/(6 E_F*) + C_rho n/(8 y^(2a)) - (1/2) C_delta n (M*/E_F*)^2 / (1 + C_delta dn_s/dM*) on the symmetric branch y(n) (exact parabolic coefficient; textbook limit Kubis-Kutschera 1997 / Liu et al. 2002: -(1/2)(g_delta/m_delta)^2 (M*/E_F*)^2 n); checked against a numerical second derivative.

caveats: Hartree (mean-field) level only. The rho tensor coupling has no Hartree contribution in homogeneous matter; Fock terms of the rho (vector and tensor), the delta and the pion are not included. In relativistic Hartree-Fock models those exchange terms carry a large, sub-linear part of the symmetry energy, which is the density dependence R1 and A1 require.

The delta couplings: the task range 1.0-1.3 is used as declared; the Bonn A/B/C values 0.7709 / 3.1155 / 5.0742 and the Bonn A sigma coupling 8.3141 are recalled from memory and could not be checked online (arxiv.org is outside this session's network allow-list). Larger delta couplings only make R1 worse (Bonn B, C give J < 5 MeV and negative).
A1 and A2 are properties of members whose isovector term was a FITTED contact (J = 32, L = 50). The test here replaces that contact; it does not add the mesons on top of it.

Skins come from published L correlations calibrated on functionals with J = 27-40 MeV; the declared combinations have J = 13-27, so the skins are extrapolations. Correlation coefficients for 48Ca from web-search snippets, not from the papers.

48Ca / 208Pb spin-orbit numbers use the session LDA procedure, which is validated on 16O 1p only (it overestimates high-l splittings of standard models: NL3 208Pb 1i 9.47 vs 5.84 MeV). Use them as changes relative to the isoscalar baseline. Experimental single-particle splittings are from memory.
16O: isospin breaking by Coulomb (n_p != n_n at the percent level) would give a rho-tensor contribution of order 0.01-0.03 MeV; not computed.
m_delta is kept at 983 MeV at all densities; a W-dependent delta mass or coupling was not declared and not computed.

The y* = 0.84 island member sits on the a5_min stability edge (float q_min = -4.4e-4); its reference run needed the stability gate relaxed to |q_min| < 1e-3 (same member as in the closure). The y* = 0.87 quartic reference has M_max = 1.79.
Stars for the declared combinations were run although J is outside the [28, 36] gate used earlier; with J this low the SLy crust match moves to 0.47-0.82 n0.
KSRF value 5.952 uses f_pi = 92.1 MeV; the 5.9-6.0 bracket changes J by -0.22..+0.21 MeV.
verdict_text: A zero-parameter isovector sector built from the known mesons at mean-field level does not close R1 and does not keep A1. The KSRF/VMD rho (g_rho = 5.95) raises S(n0) from 13.4-13.9 MeV to 22.5-22.9 MeV with a constant rho mass and to 25.4-26.7 MeV if the rho mass follows W (target 31.7 +- 3.2; best z = -1.56); it closes 50-72 percent of the J gap but only 36-47 percent of the gap at 0.10 fm^-3, where S_2 = 15.2-16.8 MeV (25.5 +- 1.0) and E_PNM/N = 1.8-3.3 MeV (11.4 +- 1.0). The delta/a0(980) moves the wrong way for any real coupling: -7.2 MeV in J per unit g_delta^2/4pi, so J = 13.1-20.1 MeV at OBE strength and neutron matter becomes bound at 0.10 fm^-3; fitting the delta coupling to J has no physical solution (g_delta^2/4pi = -0.7..-1.3), and the quark-counting coupling from the action's own scalar Yukawa is negligible (-0.08 MeV). The rho tensor coupling (kappa = 3.7) does nothing for R2: it vanishes in homogeneous matter and in N = Z nuclei, so the 16O 1p splitting stays at 1.45 / 1.04 MeV; in 48Ca and 208Pb it shifts neutron splittings up and proton splittings down by 4-29 percent, away from experiment. Stars: the joint likelihood falls from chi2 = 13.9 (p = 0.085, y084 reference) to 168-537 through the two nuclear terms; on the six stellar terms the rho alone raises R_eq(1.44) by 0.5-1.1 km (wrong way for R5) while lifting M_max by 0.07 Msun. Ground state and vacuum are unaffected. The result is constructive in one respect: R1 and A1 together require an isovector potential energy that grows as n^(0.26-0.29) near and below n0; a constant-coupling meson contact grows as n^1.0 (n^1.2-1.33 with m_rho ~ W). The delta and the rho are the only isovector mesons with a Hartree mean field (pi and a1 have none in a parity-conserving ground state), so the Hartree isovector sector is exhausted: the missing isovector element is not the delta and not a constant-coupling rho; it must weaken with density (density-dependent coupling, omega-rho cross term, or finite-range exchange). Predictions of the zero-parameter sector, for the record: K_sym = -22..-6 MeV (constant m_rho) or +14..+88 MeV (m_rho ~ W); 208Pb skin 0.184-0.189 fm (0.207-0.224), 48Ca skin 0.176-0.179 fm (0.190-0.200).
